name: Engine cooling fan impeller, high-flow shrouded WE43 magnesium concept F1
description: High-flow iteration of the F0 impeller. It replaces F0's twelve flat radial paddles with eleven twisted, cambered airfoil blades designed from velocity triangles, ties their tips to a rotating shroud with a two-tooth labyrinth, carries their roots on a 120 mm thin-walled cup hub, shrinks to 248 mm so it clears the F0 housing's 252 mm throat and fits the EOS M 290 plate, and moves to LPBF WE43 magnesium. A one-dimensional blade-element model with radial equilibrium, on the synthetic F0 engine resistance, estimates about 19 % more flow than a conventional reference rotor at the same speed. This is a model estimate on synthetic inputs, not a measurement and not a comparison with the original Porsche part.

classification.intended_use: F1 design study: airfoil blade design, one-dimensional fan-curve simulation against the synthetic engine resistance, lighter-alloy comparison and F0 housing fit; no manufacture, rotation, installation or start-up authorized

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Magnesium is anodic to steel shaft, steel fasteners and aluminium housing: coating, insulating washers and a sealed bore insert are required.

known_limits: All geometry, speeds, flow targets and the engine resistance curve are synthetic.
The flow gains come from a one-dimensional blade-element model, not CFD or a rig test.
Gains are quoted against R0, a conventional rotor designed by the same method; the original Porsche impeller's performance is unknown.

Most of the 19 % flow gain at equal speed comes from loading the blades harder, which costs about 69 % more shaft power; at equal shaft power the rotor alone gains about 0.2 %, and about 12 % with a matched stator and bellmouth.
The stator and bellmouth belong to a future housing F1 and are not part of this rotor.
WE43 data are single-laboratory room-temperature coupons plus generic values; no hot, HCF or notched allowable.
The fully constrained thermal screen fails for WE43; the free shroud makes bore loosening on the steel shaft the governing case, which needs an insert.
Support removal inside the enclosed shrouded passages is unresolved; no manufacture, rotation, installation or start-up is authorized.

The flat-fan sizing study F2 finds the best size at the synthetic duty to be 260 mm, within 0.1 % of this 248 mm wheel at equal power; at the four-times-larger duties that real flat fans suggest, the optimum reaches the 520 mm edge of the sweep.

Radial equilibrium (simple, inlet uniform) moved the hub from 80 to 120 mm: with the 80 mm hub the hub section fell to de Haller 0.58 and a station stalled; the 120 mm cup hub with a free vortex keeps every station at or above 0.75.

The shroud-clamped first blade mode (about 2,140 Hz) sits between the six-spoke order (1,000 Hz) and the seventeen-vane order (2,833 Hz), 24 % from the latter by a beam estimate; an FE Campbell diagram is required.
The cup web is closed: the alternator cooling path through the hub (twelve windows on the original Turbo rotor's visual rebuild) is not modelled.
